questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: ABUNDANT
questions.explanation: ABUNDANT means existing in large quantities; antonym = Scanty (meager, insufficient). Plentiful is a synonym. Sufficient means adequate (not strongly opposite).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: CONCEAL
questions.explanation: CONCEAL means to keep something hidden; antonym = Reveal (to make known). Hide, Cover, and Disguise are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: DILIGENT
questions.explanation: DILIGENT means hardworking; antonym = Indolent (habitually lazy). Hardworking and Industrious are synonyms. Careful is related but not opposite.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: MAGNIFY
questions.explanation: MAGNIFY means to make larger or more important; antonym = Diminish (to make smaller). Amplify, Enlarge, and Exaggerate are synonyms or related.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: OPTIMISTIC
questions.explanation: OPTIMISTIC means having a positive outlook; antonym = Pessimistic (tending to see the worst). Hopeful, Cheerful, and Confident are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: TRANSIENT
questions.explanation: TRANSIENT means lasting only for a short time; antonym = Permanent. Fleeting, Temporary, and Brief are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: VERBOSE
questions.explanation: VERBOSE means using more words than necessary; antonym = Concise (brief and to the point). Wordy, Lengthy, and Elaborate are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: ACRIMONIOUS
questions.explanation: ACRIMONIOUS means angry and bitter; antonym = Amicable (done in a friendly spirit). Bitter, Harsh, and Resentful are synonyms. Amicable often appears in 'amicable settlement' in competitive exam contexts.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: BENIGN
questions.explanation: BENIGN means gentle, kindly, or (of a tumour) not harmful; antonym = Malignant (very virulent or harmful). This is a critical medical/exam vocabulary pair.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: CLANDESTINE
questions.explanation: CLANDESTINE means kept secret or done secretively; antonym = Open (not secret). Secret, Covert, and Hidden are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: DEARTH
questions.explanation: DEARTH means a scarcity or lack of something; antonym = Abundance. Scarcity, Lack, and Shortage are synonyms. 'A dearth of ideas' = few ideas.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: FRUGAL
questions.explanation: FRUGAL means careful with money; antonym = Prodigal (spending money recklessly). Thrifty and Economical are synonyms. 'Prodigal son' = one who wastes resources.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: LACONIC
questions.explanation: LACONIC means using very few words; antonym = Garrulous (excessively talkative). Terse, Brief, and Concise are synonyms. Origin: Laconia (Sparta), where people were famous for plain speech.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: METICULOUS
questions.explanation: METICULOUS means showing great attention to detail; antonym = Careless. Careful, Precise, and Thorough are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: NONCHALANT
questions.explanation: NONCHALANT means appearing casually calm and relaxed; antonym = Concerned (anxious, worried). Casual, Unconcerned, and Indifferent are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: OPAQUE
questions.explanation: OPAQUE means not able to be seen through; antonym = Transparent. Murky, Dark, and Cloudy are synonyms or closely related.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: PLACID
questions.explanation: PLACID means not easily upset or excited, calm; antonym = Turbulent (full of confusion or disorder). Calm, Serene, and Tranquil are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: RANCOUR
questions.explanation: RANCOUR means bitterness or resentfulness, especially long-standing; antonym = Goodwill. Bitterness, Malice, and Spite are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: STOIC
questions.explanation: STOIC means enduring pain without complaint; antonym = Emotional (easily affected by feelings). Indifferent, Impassive, and Uncomplaining are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: TACITURN
questions.explanation: TACITURN means reserved or uncommunicative in speech; antonym = Verbose (using more words than necessary). Reserved, Silent, and Quiet are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: ALACRITY
questions.explanation: ALACRITY means brisk and cheerful readiness; antonym = Sluggishness. Eagerness, Readiness, and Enthusiasm are synonyms. 'With alacrity' = enthusiastically and promptly.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: INIMICAL
questions.explanation: INIMICAL means tending to obstruct or harm; unfriendly; antonym = Amiable (having a friendly and pleasant manner). Root: Latin inimicus = enemy.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: MAWKISH
questions.explanation: MAWKISH means sentimental in an exaggerated or false way; antonym = Unsentimental (not swayed by sentiment). Sentimental, Soppy, and Gushing are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: PARSIMONIOUS
questions.explanation: PARSIMONIOUS means very unwilling to spend money; excessively frugal; antonym = Generous. Miserly, Mean, and Stingy are synonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word OPPOSITE IN MEANING to: QUERULOUS
questions.explanation: QUERULOUS means complaining in a petulant or whining manner; antonym = Content (satisfied). Complaining, Whining, and Peevish are synonyms. Frequently tested in SSC CGL.
questions.subject: English
